name: Huglin Index Calculator
seoDesc: The Huglin index measures the heat available for grape ripening, weighting daytime temperatures more heavily than night ones. Free huglin index calculator: en
summary:
The Huglin index measures the heat available for grape ripening, weighting daytime temperatures more heavily than night ones. It returns contribution per day, huglin index and climate class (1 very cool … 6 too hot), and the panel shows all of them at once.

It is the standard climate index for matching a grape variety to a site, and it decides which varieties can ripen there. Press Calculate and the results appear in the grey boxes; after the first press they keep up with every edit, so there is no page to reload. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the Huglin Index
sections.html:
HI = K × [(T_max − 10) + (T_mean − 10)] ÷ 2, summed over the growing period

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
T_maxmean daily maximum°C
T_meanmean daily temperature°C
Kdaylength coefficient—
HIHuglin heliothermal index°C·day

sections.title: How do I use the Huglin Index?
sections.html:
Every input sits in the same order the formula is written, so the page reads like the equation.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: mean daily maximum of 26°C, mean daily temperature of 18°C, base temperature of 10°C, days in the growing period of 180 days, daylength coefficient (k) of 1.02.

Substituting them into the formula gives contribution per day of 12.24 °C·day, huglin index of 2,203.2, climate class (1 very cool … 6 too hot) of 4.

Those numbers come from the same solver the page runs in your browser, not from an illustration, so typing different inputs moves the answer exactly as the arithmetic says.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
The number on its own is not a judgement. These are the bands most often used when the result is quoted in a paper, a report or a label:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
below 1 500 (class 1)Very coolearly varieties only; sparkling base wines
1 500 – 1 800 (class 2)CoolPinot Noir, Chardonnay, Riesling
1 800 – 2 100 (class 3)TemperateCabernet Franc, Merlot, Sauvignon Blanc
2 100 – 2 400 (class 4)WarmCabernet Sauvignon, Syrah, Grenache
2 400 – 3 000 (class 5)Very warmlate-ripening Mediterranean varieties
above 3 000 (class 6)Too hotheat stress and irrigation become the limit

  • The formula weights the maximum temperature fully, which is what distinguishes it from growing degree days.

  • The daylength coefficient K is 1.02 below 40° latitude and 1.00 above it, correcting for longer summer days in the south.

  • Huglin is usually calculated over the frost-free period from April to September in the northern hemisphere, October to March in the south.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
These are the errors that account for almost every wrong answer people bring to this calculator:

  • Summing over a full year rather than the growing period.
  • Forgetting the K coefficient and comparing sites at different latitudes.
  • Using the Huglin index to compare varieties without checking their own heat requirements.

faq.q: What Huglin index suits Cabernet Sauvignon?
faq.a: About 2 100–2 400, which is why it struggles to ripen in cool maritime climates.

faq.q: Is Huglin better than growing degree days?
faq.a: For viticulture it usually is, because the extra weight on daytime heat matches ripening better than a plain mean.

faq.q: What does the Huglin Index actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns contribution per day, huglin index and climate class (1 very cool … 6 too hot). Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
